The runtime error code FLS_E_UNEXPECTED_FLASH_ID shall be reported when the expected flash ID is not matched (see [SWS_Fls_00144]).
The function Fls_Init shall set the FLS module state to MEMIF_IDLE after having finished the FLS module initialization.
The function Fls_Init shall set the flash job result to MEMIF_JOB_OK after having finished the FLS module initialization.
The function Fls_Erase shall copy the given parameters to FLS module internal variables and initiate an erase job.
After initiating the erase job, the function Fls_Erase shall set the FLS module status to MEMIF_BUSY.
After initiating the erase job, the function Fls_Erase shall set the job result to MEMIF_JOB_PENDING.
After initiating the erase job, the function Fls_Erase shall return with E_OK.
The function Fls_Write shall copy the given parameters to Fls module internal variables and initiate a write job.
After initiating the write job, the function Fls_Write shall set the FLS module status to MEMIF_BUSY.
After initiating the write job, the function Fls_Write shall set the job result to MEMIF_ JOB_PENDING.
After initiating the write job, the function Fls_Write shall return with E_OK.
The function Fls_Cancel shall reset the FLS module’s internal job processing variables (like address, length and data pointer).
The function Fls_Cancel shall set the FLS module state to MEMIF_IDLE.
The function Fls_Read shall copy the given parameters to FLS module internal variables and initiate a read job.
After initiating a read job, the function Fls_Read shall set the FLS module status to MEMIF_BUSY.
After initiating a read job, the function Fls_Read shall set the FLS module job result to MEMIF_JOB_PENDING.
After initiating a read job, the function Fls_Read shall return with E_OK.
The function Fls_Compare shall copy the given parameters to Fls module internal variables and initiate a compare job.
After initiating the compare job, the function Fls_Compare shall set the status to MEMIF_BUSY.
After initiating the compare job, the function Fls_Compare shall set the job result to MEMIF_JOB_PENDING.
After initiating the compare job, the function Fls_Compare shall return with E_OK.

After a read, erase, write or compare job has been finished, the function Fls_MainFunction shall set the FLS module’s job result to MEMIF_JOB_OK if it is currently in state MEMIF_JOB_PENDING. Otherwise, it shall leave the result unchanged.

After a read, erase, write or compare job has been finished, the function Fls_MainFunction shall set the FLS module’s state to MEMIF_IDLE and call the job end notification function if configured (see [ECUC_Fls_00307]).

The FLS module shall call the callback function Fee_JobErrorNotification when the module has finished a job with a negative result: • Read job failed • Write job failed • Erase job failed • Compare job failed
The FLS module shall call the callback function Fee_JobErrorNotification when the module has canceled an ongoing job: • Read job aborted • Write job aborted • Erase job aborted • Compare job aborted
The FLS module shall call the callback function Fee_JobErrorNotification when the module has finished a compare job and the memory blocks differ: • Compare job finished and memory blocks differ

The Flash test module provides test execution services in background and foreground mode.
The memory blocks to be tested shall be configurable for background and foreground mode separately.

In background mode the test blocks shall be tested in the same order they are configured in configuration structure. When all blocks are tested, one test interval is completed. In background testing the partial tests shall be triggered via FlsTst_MainFunction (see [SWS_FlsTst_00066]).

The length of a partial test is defined by the number of tested cells, which shall be tested in one scheduled task. (see [ECUC_FlsTst_00161]). The required time for a partial test without interruption is defined as "Test time".

A background test shall be aborted or suspended via the API services FlsTst_Abort() or FlsTst_Suspended(). The maximum latency time until the API call request is processed, shall be configurable (see [ECUC_FlsTst_00120]).

Foreground tests are defined as synchronous tests which shall not be interrupted. The execution of Foreground tests is configurable (see [ECUC_FlsTst_00086]) and can be called after module initialization at any time.

Feature Models may be empty A FMFeatureModel may have zero references to FMFeature elements in the role feature .

Definition of Feature A Feature describes an essential characteristic of a product. Features usually differentiate one product from similar products  in our context, features differentiate the individual products in a product line.

Definition of Feature Selection A Feature Selection is a set of Features that describes a specific product. A Feature Selection is always paired with a Feature Model . All dependencies and relations that are defined in the Feature Model shall be obeyed.

Definition of Feature Model A Feature Model describes the available features of a product line and their interrelations / interdependencies. In other words, a Feature Model describes a Product Line Model in the problem domain. For example, a car may have either a gasoline or a diesel engine, so the features Gasoline and Diesel are alternatives. A seven-seat…

Definition of Product Model A Product Model describes a product. A Product Model does not contain variation points anymore (except for PostBuild variation points). It is derived from the Product Line Model by binding the variation points. In AUTOSAR, a Product Model is a collection of M1 artifacts that describes a particular Product . Except for PostBuild…

Definition of Product Line Model A Product Line Model is similar to a Product Model , but contains variation points of all binding times. A Product Model is created out of a Product Line Model by keeping certain variations, and discarding others (i.e., binding). The only variation points that are still allowed in a Product Model are PostBuild variation poin…

Definition of Product A Product is an artifact that is the outcome of some type of process, for example a software that runs on one or more ECUs. In AUTOSAR, a Product is a collection of M0 artifacts. In our terminology, it is described by a Product Model on M1 Level.

Definition of Product Line A Product Line is a collection of Products that are related. A Product Line usually consists of a set of Products that have a certain amount of common aspects and a number of aspects that differentiate the individual Products from each other. Then the feature set of S is the set of FMFeatures ⌊ f 1 ; f 2 ; : : : ; f n g wheres i refers to f i in the role feature .
Default values for attributes min and max of FMFeatureDecomposition If min and max are missing, then the values 1 (for min ) and 1 (for max ) are assumed in [TPS_FMDT_00046].
Feature Models are optional An AUTOSAR model that does not contain a feature model is still a valid AUTOSAR model.

Definition of Parent Feature , Child Feature Let f be a FMFeature which aggregates a FMFeatureDecomposition that references a FMFeature f 0 in the role feature . Then f is the parent feature of f 0 , and f 0 is a child feature of f .

MANDATORYFEATURE All FMFeatures referenced in the role feature from a FMFeatureDecomposition that has the category MANDATORYFEATURE shall be present in a feature selection if and only if its parent FMFeature is included in the feature selection.

OPTIONALFEATURE FMFeatures referenced in the role feature from a FMFeatureDecomposition that has the category OPTIONALFEATURE may be present in a feature selection if and only if its parent FMFeature is included in the feature selection.

ALTERNATIVEFEATURE Exactly one of the FMFeatures referenced in the role feature from a FMFeatureDecomposition that has the category ALTERNATIVEFEATURE shall be present in a feature selection if and only if its parent FMFeature is included in the feature selection.

MULTIPLEFEATURE One or more of the FMFeatures referenced in the role feature from a FMFeatureDecomposition that has the category MULTIPLEFEATURE shall be present in a feature selection if and only if its parent FMFeature is included in the feature selection. This is further constrained by the attributes min and max (see [TPS_FMDT_00012] and [constr_5013]).

Name of a FMFeature The attribute shortName may be used to identify a feature. Furthermore, the attribute longName may be used to provide a human readable name for a FMFeature .
Description for a FMFeature The attributes introduction and desc may be used to provide a human readable description for a FMFeature .

Purpose of FMFeatureDecomposition Each FMFeature aggregates zero or more FMFeatureDecomposition elements in the role decomposition . FMFeatureDecomposition thus establishes a hierarchical organization of FMFeatures.
Purpose of FMFeature A FMFeature describes an essential characteristic of a product, as defined in [TPS_FMDT_00002].
Purpose of FMFeatureModel A FMFeatureModel describes the available features of a product line, as defined in [TPS_FMDT_00004].
